title: Response-Quantile Observability & Throughput Wallboard by Route/Model/Region
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a unified wallboard that correlates token throughput (tokens/sec) with response-time quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) for every route, model variant, and region.

Scope:
- Ingest benchmark-run telemetry and live production telemetry into a per-route/model/region timeseries store with quantile rollups.
- Surface an interactive dashboard/wallboard that lets SREs/engineers pivot by route, model, region, and traffic slice (e.g., prompt length buckets, batch size).
- Add per-slice regression detectors that annotate the dashboard when p95 or p99 drifts beyond historical baselines.
- Expose derived metrics for tokens/sec, requests/sec, median latency, p95, p99, and error-rate.

Design highlights:
- Use streaming aggregator to compute approximate quantiles (tdigest/CKMS) for high cardinality slices to avoid cardinality explosion.
- Store both raw histogram summaries (for short-term detailed forensics) and downsampled quantile rollups for long-term dashboards.
- Bench harness integration: accept structured outputs from load harness (bench-run metadata: synthetic vs production replay, prompt-length distribution, KV cache hit-rate) and join with runtime telemetry.
- Dashboard UX: left column shows tokens/sec and rps heatmap by region; center shows p95/p99 time-series and top offender slices; right shows recent regressions and suggested rollbacks/canary actions.

Operational requirements:
- Ingest latency: <60s for bench runs, <120s for production aggregates.
- Query/board render: <2s for pre-aggregated views; drilldowns may take longer.
- Alerting: automatic ticket creation when p95 increases by >25% vs 7d baseline and p99 increases by >15% with more than 1000 requests in the slice.

Out of scope for this ticket: automated model fallback and routing; full multi-tenant RBAC for dashboard access (will be separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard renders tokens/sec and p50/p90/p95/p99 for selected route/model/region within query SLAs
Bench harness (bench-run) metadata is joined with quantile rollups for at least two built-in slices: prompt-length and batch-size
Regression annotations appear on the wallboard when thresholds are crossed and a sample alert ticket is created (test mode)
Documentation with runbook and walkthrough is published in Confluence and linked from the dashboard
Load on metrics ingestion pipeline remains within 20% of baseline after enabling quantile rollups (validated with synthetic load)

notes: This ticket intentionally keeps cardinality low by limiting mandatory pivot dimensions to route|model|region and optional slices (prompt-length, batch-size). If additional high-cardinality slices are required, we'll add sampled drilldown pipelines. Plan to hand off long-term storage retention policy to Observability team after launch.
